belief: If I miss God’s perfect will, my life is ruined.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if you miss God’s perfect will your life is ruined, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that God has one exact plan and missing it means settling for second best forever. Regret over a past decision, such as a job, a move, or a marriage. Fear of making the wrong choice. Perfectionism. Hearing people talk about being “out of God’s will.”
teaches: God is sovereign and good, and He is not limited by our mistakes. When the potter’s clay was marred, he formed it into another vessel. God works all things together for good for those who love Him, even our poor choices. The LORD will fulfill His purpose for you. A person plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps. Your life is not ruined by one decision; it is in the hands of a faithful God.
self_statements: I made the wrong choice, and now my life is ruined.
If I make the wrong decision, everything is over.
I’ll never get back on track.
errors: Believing one decision has ruined everything.
Believing you are either perfectly in God’s will or permanently out of it.
Picturing God as unable to work through your mistakes.
Replaying past decisions without moving forward.
questions: What did the potter do with the marred vessel?
Who will fulfill His purpose for me, according to Psalm 138:8?
Is God’s plan so fragile that I can ruin it?
What can I learn from the past and do faithfully today?
What would change if I trusted God with my past decisions?
truth: Missing God’s best in a decision does not ruin my life. God is not limited by my mistakes. Like a potter reshaping clay, He can form something good from my life. He works all things together for my good and will fulfill His purpose for me. I can learn, repent where needed, and walk faithfully today.
hw_questions: What did the potter do with marred clay?

hw_truths: God is not limited by my mistakes.
God works all things together for good.
The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me.

God will finish what He started in me.
log: Each day, write one faithful step I took today, without dwelling on past decisions.
name_example: The LORD will fulfill His purpose for Sarah. O LORD, Your loving devotion endures forever—do not abandon the works of Your hands.

prayer: Father, thank You that You are not limited by my mistakes. Help me reject the lie that missing Your perfect will has ruined my life. Reshape my life as You see best, work all things together for good, and help me walk faithfully with You today. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
